targets.authors: Cook J, Lewandowsky S, Ecker UKH
targets.title: Neutralizing misinformation through inoculation: Exposing misleading argumentation techniques reduces their influence.
targets.evidence_quote: Following these arguments, this study replicates one of the experiments conducted by Cook et al. (2017) for Germany and extends their study by including further intervening variables (populist attitudes, political orientation), for which other studies have found an influence on climate-related attitudes (for a summary, see Cook, 2016).
targets.outcome_quote: Regarding the effects of misinformation messages and most notably the effects of inoculation messages, we could not replicate the findings of Cook et al. (2017); At least in our setting, the misinformation message and also inoculation preceding misinformation had hardly any effect on the climate-related attitudes under study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report failure for the misinformation and inoculation effects central to the title and design. Confirmation of pre-existing worldview associations does not establish the experimental effects. The stated limitations are explanations rather than an uninformative verdict.

reasoning: A German sample re-tests Experiment 2 of Cook et al. (2017). Other studies supply background or measurements, not independent targets.
